clue.text: Questionable brief moment when Juliet wanders away

indicators.note: something that wanders away is no longer present, so 'Juliet' leaves the brief moment

parts.note: a jiffy is a very short moment
Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A fleeting romantic moment turns doubtful when Juliet drifts off, as if Romeo has been left standing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take J from JIFFY. 'Brief' is part of the definition of the moment, not a truncation signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or dubious, a straightforward synonym for questionable.

clue.text: Giving a quality to Mev's search engine takes one third of CPU

parts.note: Mev is the setter, so 'Mev's' is 'I'm' from the setter's viewpoint

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so the search engine takes the letter inside itself

parts.note: Microsoft's search engine

indicators.note: the abbreviation has three letters, so one third of it is a single letter, here its last

parts.note: the third letter of the three

explanation.surface: Something about the setter's own search engine is being given character by grabbing a chunk of a computer processor.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use their own pseudonym to mean I or ME, so a setter's name with 's reads as 'I'm'. The processor's letter sits inside the engine's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to fill or inspire with a feeling or characteristic, so imbuing means instilling some trait in something.

clue.text: Father due to reform complex bloke?

parts.note: Fr. is the abbreviation for Father, the priest's title

indicators.note: reforming something rebuilds it in a new shape, so the letters of 'due' are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, three letters

explanation.surface: A priest is meant to straighten out a troubled, complicated man.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: 'complex bloke' reads like a complicated man, but it means the man of complexes, the Oedipus complex's inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund Freud, founder of psychoanalysis, named the Oedipus and other psychological complexes, so he is the man famed for them.

clue.text: Ancient corrupter of youth reacts so egregiously

indicators.note: acting egregiously means behaving outrageously out of line, so the letters misbehave out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: An old man accused of leading the young astray responds outrageously to the charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egregiously' is an unusual anagram signal, but it means outrageously, which is exactly how he was charged with behaving.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian philosopher was tried and executed on charges including corrupting the youth of the city, so the description is his indictment.

clue.text: Non-heinous to accept extremely inhuman noise from 25 on the farm?

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so 'Non-heinous' holds the ends of 'inhuman'

parts.note: not heinous means acceptable, all right

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outside letters of 'inhuman' count

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something mild is asked to put up with a cruel, inhuman racket out in the farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 across is NAPOLEON, the pig who rules Orwell's Animal Farm, so his farm noise is a pig's grunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's grunt is written as oink, and Orwell's Napoleon is a pig on Animal Farm, hence the cross-reference.

clue.text: Tease avant-garde composer for symmetrical part of his structure

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them
John Cage, the American experimental composer of 4'33"

explanation.surface: Mocking an experimental composer for the neat symmetry of how he builds his music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His structure' sounds like the composer's musical form, but it means a man's skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: The ribcage is the paired, mirror-image framework of bones in the chest, a symmetrical piece of the human skeleton.

clue.text: Inform Geller (an inhabitant of Earth)

parts.note: to inform is to tell
Uri Geller, the Israeli spoon-bending entertainer
used as it stands

explanation.surface: Someone tips off Uri Geller, a bracketed aside reminding us he is only human.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'an' does double duty in the surface but in the wordplay simply supplies its own letters, before the definition takes over.
explanation.definitionFit: Tellurian comes from Latin tellus, the ground or world, and names a dweller on our planet, as opposed to an alien.

clue.text: Dorothy's speakers

definitions.note: the clue asks for Dorothy's surname, a noun, not a possessive
definitions.meaning: the surname of Dorothy L., the English detective novelist who created Lord Peter Wimsey

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dorothy's' reads as belonging to Dorothy, but it asks for her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who utter words are sayers, and Dorothy L. Sayers was a famous crime novelist, giving two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Primarily shunning hijabs, Iranian ladies overthrow hierarchy in historic battle

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so each word gives up its opening letter

parts.words: shunning hijabs, Iranian ladies overthrow hierarchy
parts.note: the initials of the six words

explanation.surface: Iranian women throwing off their headscarves and the ruling order in a famous uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a strong political story, which hides that only the initials matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiloh was a bloody 1862 American Civil War engagement in Tennessee, a well-known battle of history.

clue.text: Seen Cave tragically fade from memory

indicators.note: a tragic turn wrecks things, so the letters of 'Seen Cave' are ruined and rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: Nick Cave's tragic songs fade from the memory once they are over.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Cave, the Australian singer, is a surface decoy; the name is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To evanesce is to vanish gradually, like vapour, so it matches slipping away and disappearing from recollection.

clue.text: Pastoral fellow's worker emptied trench cooker

parts.note: a worker bee; worker is a standard crossword clue for bee or ant

indicators.note: an emptied container keeps only its shell, so just the outside letters of 'trench' survive

parts.note: first and last letters
an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: A country farmhand's labourer cleans out a ditch and a stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pastoral fellow' seems to be a shepherd, but it is the man who wrote the Pastoral Symphony; the 's means 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven composed the Sixth Symphony, subtitled the Pastoral, so he is the man identified by that work.

clue.text: Caprine outlaw?

parts.note: surface reading: a goat that has broken the law
setter's reading: a famous Wild West gunman whose nickname is made of two words for goats

explanation.walkthrough: Caprine means goat-like. A billy is a male goat and a kid a young one, so the Wild West outlaw's name is doubly goatish.
explanation.definitionFit: The American frontier gunman William Bonney was known by this nickname, and both halves are names for goats.

clue.text: Cool Monkee detailed Tork initially being lazy

indicators.note: de-tailed means with the tail cut off, so the Monkee loses his last letter

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
Micky Dolenz, drummer and singer of the Monkees, without his final letter

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of 'Tork' is taken

parts.note: Peter Tork, another Monkee; first letter only

explanation.surface: A laid-back member of the Monkees gives a detailed account of bandmate Tork slacking off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'in detail' but splits as de-tailed: DOLENZ loses its Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolent describes someone idle and averse to effort, a direct synonym for lazy.

clue.text: Placing a short sentry near Jack's car

indicators.note: something cut short is missing its end, so the sentry loses its final letter
placing one thing by another sets pieces side by side, starting the instruction that ends at 'near'
near means right next to, so the shortened guard with its article sits beside the card

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
used as it stands
a sentry is a guard; shortened

explanation.surface: Someone posts a guard next to Jack's motor to keep it safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Placing ... near' tells you to put A GUAR beside J; the J comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaguar is a British luxury motor manufacturer, so a Jaguar is a make of automobile.

clue.text: "Marauder" content to thank Ken Higgs for an upset

indicators.note: upsetting things knocks them over into disorder, so the gathered letters are rearranged
a word's content is what sits inside it, so 'thank' gives only its middle letters

parts.note: the inside of the word, without its first and last letters
anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: A raider is quite happy to say thanks to Ken Higgs, a former England fast bowler, for an unexpected defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like the adjective happy but means the contents of 'thank'. Ken Higgs was an England cricketer; his name is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mongol conqueror led devastating raids and invasions across Asia, making him the archetypal plunderer and raider.

clue.text: Residents' peculiar slant surrounding Scottish island

indicators.note: to surround is to go all round, so the rearranged letters sit either side of the island
peculiar means odd or strange, so 'slant' is put into an odd order

parts.note: anagram fodder, five letters
Iona, the small island in the Inner Hebrides famous for its abbey

explanation.surface: Locals have an odd take on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Residents' looks like it wants a word for inhabitants of the island itself, but it defines the whole answer; the scrambled letters split in two around the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationals are citizens of a country, people who belong there, loosely those who live in it.

clue.text: See 11
Potty war involved this political system

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of 'Potty war' are twisted together

parts.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: A silly squabble is what this kind of politics involves.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a dig: politics dominated by two big parties looks like a daft war.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-party system is one where government alternates between two dominant parties, as in the US.

clue.text: Cry from Jay, possibly about whiskey

parts.note: ca. is circa, Latin for about
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone called Jay grumbles about whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jay' looks like a person's name but is the bird, with 'possibly' marking it as one example of the crow family.
explanation.definitionFit: The jay belongs to the crow family, whose harsh call is written as a caw.

clue.text: Small piece of furniture is not wobbly

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A little side table that stands firm, reassuringly.
explanation.walkthrough: S is small, as on clothing sizes, and 'is' just joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable means firmly fixed and steady, the opposite of shaky or likely to tip over.

clue.text: Italian city and French port contracted spies

indicators.note: a contracted word is shortened, so the French port loses its last letter

parts.note: Brest, the naval port in Brittany, without its final letter
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: An Italian and a French town have hired spies on contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' reads as hired but means shortened, and applies to the port only.
explanation.definitionFit: Brescia is a city in Lombardy in northern Italy, between Milan and Lake Garda.

clue.text: Relating to sequence from actor Dina Lohan

indicators.note: taken from means extracted out of, so the letters come straight out of the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the end of 'actor', all of 'Dina' and the start of 'Lohan'

explanation.surface: A comment on a sequence performed by an actor, with Lindsay Lohan's mother Dina named.
explanation.walkthrough: Dina Lohan is Lindsay Lohan's mother, a name chosen for the letters it lends.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinal numbers such as first, second and third denote position in a series rather than quantity.

clue.text: Musical style reflected river and trees

indicators.note: a mirror reflection flips left and right, so the joined words run backwards

parts.note: the Po, Italy's longest river
a wood is a collection of trees

explanation.surface: A style of music seen mirrored in a river beside the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The Po is the default river in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Doo-wop is a vocal harmony genre of 1950s American rhythm and blues, named from its nonsense syllables.

clue.text: Abraham's city

definitions.note: the clue asks for Abraham's surname, a noun, not a possessive
definitions.meaning: the surname of Abraham, the sixteenth US president
the cathedral city in the east of England that gave its name to a county

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a city belonging to Abraham, perhaps Ur of the Bible; in fact 'Abraham's' asks for a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The US president's surname is shared with the English cathedral city in Lincolnshire, so both senses fit one word.

clue.text: Louise tolerates streams

definitions.note: a first name standing for the surname
definitions.meaning: the surname of Louise, the 1920s American silent film star
to brook is to put up with, as in 'brook no argument'
a brook is a small stream

explanation.surface: Louise puts up with the little rivers around her.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: each of the three words means the answer on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Brook as a verb means allow or tolerate, as a noun means a small stream, and Brooks is the silent-film actor's surname.

clue.text: Entrenched Republican suggested removing leader

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter, and removing it beheads the word for suggested

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
mooted means suggested or raised for discussion, minus its first letter

explanation.surface: A dug-in Republican proposed ousting the party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: MOOTED loses its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rooted is firmly established and hard to dislodge, exactly as something entrenched is.

clue.text: Emperor has snooze by old Spanish city

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
O is the standard abbreviation for old
León, a city in north-west Spain

explanation.surface: An emperor takes forty winks beside an ancient Spanish city while on campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peninsular War setting suits: Napoleon's armies fought across Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself ruler of France in 1804, the most famous of French emperors.

clue.text: Fresher at Oxford inspires legendary poetic woman

indicators.note: read as in-spires, the phrase has the answer sitting inside it

parts.note: runs across the end of 'Fresher', all of 'at' and the start of 'Oxford'

explanation.surface: A first-year student at Oxford is inspired by a mythical female poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspires' fits a Muse perfectly, while also hinting at Oxford's dreaming spires. A fresher is a university first-year.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry, a mythological figure who inspires verse.

clue.text: See 14
See 31
Contentious issue about a stew and the skin of tomato

parts.note: Lancashire hotpot, a British stew of meat topped with sliced potatoes
used as it stands

indicators.note: a skin is the outer layer, so only the outside letters of 'tomato' are kept

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A kitchen row over a casserole and some tomato skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen words disguise a political idiom; 'about' merely joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a delicate, controversial matter that nobody wants to handle.

clue.text: Keeps going with bogus SAS units

indicators.note: bogus means fake, not the real thing, so the letters of 'SAS units' are a false arrangement

parts.note: anagram fodder, eight letters; the SAS is the British special forces regiment

explanation.surface: Fake special forces squads somehow carry on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service; its initials here only supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to maintain it or keep it going over time, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Visionary woman and sweetheart regularly paint on flat rock

parts.note: jo is an old Scots word for a sweetheart

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the phrase is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A woman with visions and her beloved daub pictures on a flat stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo for sweetheart is Scots, from Burns's 'John Anderson, my jo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan of Arc said she heard the voices of saints and saw visions, which led her to fight for France.
